examples.question: What are the modern ways of paying for things without cash?
examples.answer: Good observation question! Today, Nigerians pay for many things without carrying cash. Bank transfers move money from one account to another using a phone app or USSD codes. ATM or debit cards allow you to pay in shops using a POS machine, the small device you see with traders and POS agents. Mobile money and payment apps let people send and receive money quickly. These methods are fast and safer than carrying plenty of cash, but they must be used carefully: never share your PIN or password with anyone. Cashless payment is part of our modern financial system!

examples.question: How should I take care of naira notes?
examples.answer: Very responsible question! The naira is a national symbol, so we must handle it with respect and care. Do not squeeze, tear or rumple naira notes; keep them flat and neat in a purse or wallet. Do not write or draw on the notes. Do not spray or stamp on naira at parties; it is actually against the law to abuse the naira. Keep money away from water, oil and dirty places. Torn and dirty notes have to be replaced, which costs the country money. Handling the naira well shows you are a patriotic Nigerian. Take care of our money!

examples.question: What are national values?
examples.answer: Great question! National values are the good behaviours and beliefs that help Nigeria grow strong, peaceful and united. They are the things we hold dear as a country. Examples include honesty, hard work, discipline, respect, patriotism, tolerance, fairness and unity. When citizens practise these values, the country moves forward: people trust one another, work gets done well, and everyone lives in peace. When people ignore them, we see cheating, laziness and quarrels. National values start with each person, including you in Primary 4! Practise honesty and hard work today, and you are already building Nigeria!

examples.question: What is patriotism?
examples.answer: Well done for asking! Patriotism means love for your country and readiness to serve and defend it. A patriotic Nigerian is proud of Nigeria, respects the national flag, sings the national anthem with respect, and says the national pledge with a full heart. Patriotism is also shown through actions: obeying the laws, keeping our environment clean, paying taxes when we grow up, supporting Nigerian-made goods, and cheering our teams like the Super Eagles. Even reporting people who destroy public property is patriotism. Loving Nigeria means helping to make her better every day. Be proud to be Nigerian!

examples.question: Why is honesty important?
examples.answer: Lovely question! Honesty means telling the truth, not stealing, not cheating, and keeping your promises. Honesty is important because it builds trust: when you are honest, your parents, teachers and friends can rely on you. An honest pupil does not copy during tests, returns money or items found on the floor, and admits mistakes instead of lying. In the bigger society, honest workers and leaders make the country rich and fair, while dishonest ones spoil things for everybody. People may forget many things about you, but they never forget whether you are honest. Choose honesty always; it is precious!

examples.question: What does respect mean and how do I show it?
examples.answer: Good question! Respect means honouring other people and treating them well, recognising their worth and their rights. In Nigeria, respect is a treasured value in all our cultures. You show respect by greeting your elders properly, the way your culture teaches, perhaps kneeling, bowing or using respectful words like sir and ma. You show it by listening when others speak, obeying parents and teachers, not insulting or mocking people, and caring for those younger than you. Respect also means valuing people of other religions, languages and tribes. Remember: respect is reciprocal; when you give it, you receive it!

examples.question: What is tolerance and why do we need it in Nigeria?
examples.answer: Wonderful question! Tolerance means accepting and respecting people who are different from us, in religion, language, tribe or opinion, and living peacefully with them. Nigeria has more than 250 ethnic groups, including Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo, Fulani, Ijaw, Kanuri, Tiv and many more, with different religions and customs. Without tolerance, these differences could cause quarrels and fighting. With tolerance, our differences become our beauty and strength. You practise tolerance by making friends from other tribes and religions, not mocking anyone's language or beliefs, and settling disagreements with words, not fists. Unity in diversity makes Nigeria great!

examples.question: What are the national symbols of Nigeria?
examples.answer: Great question! National symbols are special signs that represent Nigeria and remind us of our unity. The national flag is green, white and green: green stands for our rich agriculture and the white stands for peace and unity. The national anthem is the song we sing at important events, and the national pledge is our promise to be faithful, loyal and honest to Nigeria. The coat of arms carries the eagle for strength, two horses for dignity, and the black shield for our fertile soil. Others include the Naira, our currency, and the national passport. Always treat these symbols with respect!

examples.question: How can a Primary 4 pupil practise national values?
examples.answer: I love this question! You do not need to be an adult to build Nigeria. Practise honesty: do not cheat in tests and return anything you find that is not yours. Practise patriotism: sing the anthem proudly and keep your school and street clean. Small daily actions from millions of children build a great nation!

examples.question: What happens when citizens do not practise good values?
examples.answer: Very thoughtful question! When citizens abandon good values, the whole country suffers. Dishonesty brings cheating, stealing and corruption, so money meant for roads, hospitals and schools disappears. Laziness and indiscipline mean work is done poorly or not at all. Disrespect and intolerance cause quarrels, fighting and even violence between groups. Lack of patriotism makes people destroy public property, litter everywhere, and refuse to obey laws. Life then becomes harder for everybody, especially children. But the good news is that change starts with each person choosing good values. Be the change, and encourage your friends to join you!

examples.question: What should I do if there is an accident at home or school?
examples.answer: Very important question! If an accident happens, stay calm and do not panic. First, call an adult immediately: a parent, teacher or any trusted grown-up nearby. Do not try to treat a serious injury yourself. If someone is bleeding a little, a clean cloth can be pressed gently on the cut while you wait for help. Do not move a person who has fallen badly, because moving them wrongly can cause more harm. Keep other children away from danger, like broken glass or fire. Remember: shout for help, stay calm, and let adults handle it. You could save a life!

examples.question: What are the important emergency phone numbers I should know?
examples.answer: Well done for asking! Every child should know these numbers. The national emergency number in Nigeria is 112; it is free to call from any network, even without airtime, and connects you to the police, fire service and ambulance. You should also memorise the phone number of your parent or guardian, so you can reach them if you are lost or in trouble. Some states have their own emergency lines too, like 767 in Lagos. Only call these numbers for real emergencies; calling to play is wrong and can block help from reaching someone in danger. Write 112 in your exercise book today!

examples.question: What should I do if I get lost in a market or a strange place?
examples.answer: Good question, this can happen to anyone! If you get lost, first stop walking and stay calm; do not wander further, because moving around makes it harder for your family to find you. Look around for a safe helper: a police officer, a security guard, a market leader, or a mother with children. Tell them your name, your parents' names and their phone number if you know it. This is why memorising a parent's phone number is so important. Never follow a stranger who promises to take you home, and never enter a stranger's car. Stay where people can see you. Stay safe!

examples.question: How can I stay safe on the road?
examples.answer: Very wise question! Road safety saves lives every day. Always look left, look right, and look left again before crossing the road, and cross only when it is clear. Use the zebra crossing or pedestrian bridge where there is one. Never play, run or push your friends on or near the road. Walk on the side of the road facing oncoming vehicles, so you can see cars coming. Obey traffic lights and the traffic warden. Do not chase a ball onto the road; let an adult help you get it. In a vehicle, sit properly and do not put your head or hands outside the window. Be road-wise!

examples.question: What should I do if there is a fire?
examples.answer: Very important question! If you see a fire, shout 'Fire! Fire!' to alert everyone, and leave the building quickly through the nearest safe exit. Do not stop to pick your bag or toys; your life is worth more than any property. Do not hide under beds or inside cupboards. If the room is smoky, bend low or crawl, because cleaner air stays near the floor. If your clothes catch fire, remember: stop, drop and roll on the ground to put it out. Once outside, stay out, and let adults call the fire service on 112. Never play with matches, lighters, candles or petrol. Fire is not a toy!

examples.question: Who can I ask for help when I feel unsafe?
examples.answer: This is a very important question, and I am glad you asked! Every child has the right to protection, and you should never suffer in silence. If you feel unsafe or someone is hurting you or touching you wrongly, tell a trusted adult immediately: your parents, your class teacher, the headteacher, a school counsellor, or a religious leader you trust. If the first person does not listen, tell another one; keep telling until someone helps you. You can also call 112 in an emergency. You are never at fault for reporting, and telling is not being a bad child; it is being brave and wise. You deserve to be safe!

examples.question: How can I avoid danger from strangers?
examples.answer: Very wise question! Most people are good, but we must still be careful with strangers. Never collect sweets, biscuits, money or gifts from someone you do not know. Never follow a stranger anywhere, even if they say your mummy sent them; families should agree on a secret word for real emergencies. Never enter a stranger's car or house. Do not tell strangers your home address or when your parents are away. Walk to and from school with friends or trusted adults, and use busy roads, not lonely paths. If a stranger grabs you, shout loudly and run to where people are. Always tell your parents about any stranger who approaches you!

examples.question: Why should I not play with electricity?
examples.answer: Excellent safety question! Electricity is very useful, but it can injure or even kill when handled carelessly. Never push your fingers, pencils, spoons or wires into electric sockets. Do not touch switches, sockets or electrical appliances with wet hands, because water carries electric current easily. Do not fly kites near electric wires, and never touch a fallen electric cable on the road; report it to an adult at once. If an appliance sparks or smells like it is burning, move away and tell an adult immediately. Let only adults and electricians handle electrical repairs. Respect electricity and it will serve you safely!
